To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the main opportunities offered by SDNs in wireless infrastructureless networks are: (i) the possibility of using the same software for managing both wireless and wired communications and (ii) the ability to dynamically adapt the network configuration to the specific requirements of the wireless devices.

SDN can provide a number of benefits to wireless infrastructureless networks (e.g., WPAN) and that the main challenge in adapting SDN to such environments is to deal with the dynamicity of the topology and of the network resources.
SDWN is feasible and that it can offer several advantages over the traditional approach to WPAN management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can the benefits offered by SDN be exploited in wireless infrastructureless networks?
the following questions.
how SDN can help to improve wireless infrastructureless networks and what is the impact of the wireless nature of the network on the design of an SDN-based wireless infrastructureless network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDWNs are a promising and viable approach to the management of WPANs, but further work is needed to validate this statement.
SDWN is not a straightforward application of SDN to the wireless domain but it requires a deep understanding of both SDN and the peculiarities of wireless networks.

, although SDN is a promising technology for the management of wireless infrastructureless networks, there is still much research to be done in order to fully exploit its capabilities in this context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SDN paradigm, if appropriately adapted, can be very beneficial to the management of wireless infrastructureless networks.

SDWNs can offer the same advantages of SDNs but with the additional benefit of providing the network with the capability to autonomously adapt its behavior according to the current context of the network.

, in order to benefit from SDN in wireless infrastructureless environments, the network should be organized in a hierarchical fashion with the SDN controller being located at the top level of the hierarchy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SDWN is a promising solution to unbridle the full power of SDN in wireless infrastructureless communications.

SDN can be a valuable asset for infrastructureless networking environments, but its benefits are limited by the fact that SDN was designed to manage wired infrastructure networks and not to manage the wireless infrastructureless networking environment.
SDN is an enabling technology for WPANs and that it can be beneficial for both the network operator and the user.
